review_method: Read all106 complete actual source units in Deuteronomy17–21, every retained target passage and necessary surrounding context in Deuteronomy1/2/4/5/7/10/12/13/24/27/28/31, Exodus14/18/20/21/23, Leviticus7/18/19/22/24, Numbers18/19/35, 1Samuel8/10, 1Kings10/11, Genesis29/49, Joshua1/10, Judges7, Matthew18/27, Acts3/6/7 and Galatians3. Separately displayed and read all113 complete source/target/category/rationale triples in three untruncated groups; separately reread the two corrected final triples. Retain actual priestly cuts and beneficiary distinctions, purification-by-fire wording, prophetic tests, accident versus hostile killing, city categories, heifer sinew-cutting, captive-woman provisions, hated-wife firstborn entitlement and body-disposal instruction. The particular local question/answer, condition/consequence, contrast and repeated-list dependencies are explicitly Same-chapter, rather than counted as independent historical fulfillment. Ancient legal textual comparisons do not assert a present-day prescription.
pin_method: Freshly fetched all12 complete raw source-book files at fixed commit, rehashed every Git blob against existing source registries and verified complete parsed equality with caches. Rehashed saved raw files and their SHA256 receipts. Cache newline and terminal-LF differences are distinguished from parsed equality.

old_row.relationship: Egyptian horse acquisition contrasted with royal restriction
old_row.rationale: The ruler must not multiply horses by returning the people to Egypt; Kings records Solomon's horses and chariot trade from Egypt, without saying this account explicitly narrates a return of the people.

new_row.relationship: Egyptian horse acquisition contrasted with royal restriction
new_row.rationale: The ruler must not multiply horses and must not return the people to Egypt to acquire them; Kings records Solomon's Egyptian horse and chariot trade, without explicitly narrating a return of the people.

old_row.relationship: Firstborn described as beginning of the children
old_row.rationale: Both describe the firstborn as the beginning of the father's children; Deuteronomy additionally prescribes his double portion and forbids displacing him through preference for his mother.

new_row.relationship: Firstborn described as beginning of the children
new_row.rationale: Both describe the firstborn as the beginning of the father's children; Deuteronomy additionally prescribes his double portion and forbids displacing the hated wife's firstborn through preference for the loved wife's son.

author_corrections.reason: Keep the two horse restrictions distinct and correct the maternal-preference referent in the firstborn explanation; no targets or counts changed.

candidate_exclusions.proposed_claim: Use Jeremiah28:7-9 as the familiar fulfilled-prophecy peace test.
candidate_exclusions.reason: Actual pinned Jeremiah28:7-9 concerns Babylon, not that prophecy test. The imported numbering is not retained and adds no pair credit.

candidate_exclusions.proposed_claim: Retain 1Kings11:1-4 as a complete ordinary four-unit range or1Kings10:26-29 without its continuation unit.
candidate_exclusions.reason: The actual first range lacks11:3, while the second contains10:26a. Retained evidence uses11:4,10:27 and10:28-29 with exact complete units; no alternate numbering is substituted.

candidate_exclusions.proposed_claim: Identify Pilate as innocent, equate his washing with the heifer ritual, infer Og-era sites or modern animal-body parts beyond the supplied wording.
candidate_exclusions.reason: The retained comparisons distinguish claims, procedures and specified text; no independent historical, linguistic, geographical or ritual equivalence verification is claimed.

editorial_notes.note: Preserve the capital witness rule, difficult-case authorities, chosen Israelite ruler, separate horse/Egypt restrictions, royal wives and wealth warnings, and the ruler-written second law. 1Kings evidence keeps actual gaps and continuation numbering without importing an absent11:3.

Preserve foreleg/cheeks/stomach versus Leviticus breast/right-foreleg portions, Aaron/Levite addressee differences, ancestral-sale qualification, purification-by-fire and divination wording, and the different prophetic tests. Acts quotations retain their speakers and differing judgment formulation.

Preserve conditional refuge expansion, nonhostile accidents versus intentional ambush, inherited boundaries, multiple witnesses and the false-witness penalty; Exodus pregnancy wording remains as supplied. Keep far cities distinct from inherited nations, distinct new-house/vineyard/marriage/fear exemptions, actual Judges7 place names, and food-tree versus nonfood-tree siege rules.

The heifer has its sinews cut in the rough unworked ravine; do not substitute neck-breaking. Handwashing parallels do not endorse Pilate innocence. Preserve the full mourning month, no-sale restriction, the hated-wife firstborn double portion, persistent rebellious-son conditions, and hanging after death with same-day removal. Galatians is explicitly a later Christological quotation/application.
